source_text: 1. Trapirionem itaque Apostolorum in toto mundo manifestatam, in omni Ecclesia adest perspicere omnibus qui vera velint videre, et habemus annumerare eos qui ab Apostolis instituti sunt Episcopi in ecclesiis, et successiones eorum usque ad nos, qui nihil tale docuerunt, neque cognoverunt, quale ab his deliratur. Etenim si recondita mysteria scissent Apostoli, que seorsim et latenter ab reliquis perfectos docebant, his vel maxime traderent ea quibus etiam ipsas ecclesias committebant. Valde enim fectos et irreprehensibiles in omnibus eos volebant esse, quos et successores relinquebant, suum ipsorum locum magisterii tradenemendate agentibus fieret magna utilitas, lapsis autem summa calamitas, Sed quoniam valde longum est, in hoe tali volumine omnium ecclesiarum enumerare successiones, maximz, et antiquissimz, et omnibus cognitz, a gloriosissimis duobus Apostolis ? Petro et Paulo Rome fundatz et constitute ecclesiz, eam quam habet ab Apostolis traditionem, et annuntiatam hominibus fidem, per successiones Episcoporum pervenientem .usque ad nos indicantes, confundimus omnes eos, qui quoquo modo vel per sibiplacentiam malam, vel vanam gloriam, vel per cecitatem et malam sententiam, preeterquam oportet colligunt. Ad hane enim ecclesiam propter potentiorem principalitatem necesse est omnem Sconvenire Ecclesiam, hoc est, eos qui sunt undique fideles, in qua semper ab his, qui sunt undique, conservata est ea que est ab Apostolis traditio. pena. Aiadexeras de avrov 2. Fundantes igitur et instruentes beati Apostoli Ecclesiam, Lino episcopatum administrande Ecclesiz tradiderunt. Hujus Lini Paulus in his que sunt ad Timotheum epistolis meminit. Succedit autem ei Anacletus: post eum tertio loco ab Apostolis episcopatum sortitur Clemens, qui et vidit ipsos Apostolos, et contulit cum eis, et cum adhuc insonantem preedicationem A postolorum et traditionem ante oculos haberet; non solus; adhuc enim multi supererant tune ab Apostolis docti.. Sub hoe igitur mente, dissensione non modica inter eos qui Corinthi essent fratres facta, scripsit quae est Romze Ecélesia potentissimas literas Corinthiis, ad pacem eos congregans, et reparans fidem eorum, et annuntians quam in recenti ab Apostolis acceperat traditionem, annuntiantem unum Deum omnipotentem, factorem cceli et terre, plasmatorem hominis, qui induxerit cataclysmum, et advocaverit Abraham, qui eduxerit populum de terra A®gypti, qui collocutus sit Moysi, qui legem disposuerit, et prophetas miserit, qui ignem preeparaverit diabolo et angelis ejus. Hune Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi ab ecclesiis annuntiari, ex ipsa scriptura, qui velint discere possunt, et apostolicam Ecclesize traditionem intelligere, cum sit vetustior epistola his qui nune falso docent, et alterum Deum super Demiurgum et factorem horum omnium que sunt commentiuntur, 8. Huie autem Clementi succedit Euaristus, et Euaristo Alexander, ac deinceps sextus ab Apostolis constitutus est Sixtus, et ab hoc Telesphorus, qui etiam gloriosissime martyrium fecit: ac deinceps Hyginus, post Pius, post quem Anicetus. Cum autem successisset Aniceto Soter, nunc duodecimo loco Episcopatum ab Apostolis habet Eleutherius. Hac ordinatione et successione ea quee est ab Apostolis in Ecclesia traditio et veritatis praeconatio Et est plenissima hee ostensio, unam et pervenit usque ad nos. eandem vivificatricem fidem esse, quae in Ecclesia ab Apostolis usque nunc sit conservata, et tradita in veritate> 4. Et Polycarpus autem non solum ab Apostolis edoctus, et conversatus cum multis ex eis qui Dominum nostrum viderunt ; sed etiam ab Apostolis in Asia, in ea que est Smyrnis Ecclesia constitutus Episcopus, quem et nos vidimus in prima nostra eetate, multum enim perseveravit, et valde senex gloriosissime et nobilissime martyrium faciens exivit de hac vita, heee docuit semper quie ab Apostolis didicerat, quee et Ecclesiz tradidit, et sola sunt vera. estimonium his perhibent que sunt in Asia ecclesi omnes, et qui usque adhuc successerunt Polycarpo: qui vir multo majoris auctoritatis, et fidelior veritatis est testis, quam Valentinus et Marcion, et reliqui qui sunt perversze sententiz. Is enim est qui sub Aniceto cum advenisset in urbem, multos ex his quos preediximus, hzereticos convertit in Ecclesiam Dei, unam et solam hane veritatem annuntians ab Apostolis percepisse se, quam et Keclesize tradidit. Et sunt qui audierunt eum®, quoniam Johannes Domini discipulus in Epheso iens lavari, cum vidisset intus Cerinthum, exsilierit de balneo non lotus, dicens, quod timeat ne balneum concidat, cum intus esset Cerinthus inimicus veritatis. Et ipse autem Polycarpus Marcioni aliquando occurrenti sibi, et dicenti, Cognoscis nos? respondit: Cognosco te primogenitum Satan. Tantum Apostoli et horum discipuli habuerunt timorem, Sut neque verbo tenus communicarent alicui eorum qui adulteraverant veritatem, quemadmodum et Paulus ait: Hareticum autem hominem post unam correptionem devita, sciens quoniam perversus est qui est talis, et est a semetipso damnatus, Est autem et epistola Polycarpi ad Philippenses scripta perfectissima, ex qua et characterem fidei ejus, et preedicationem veritatis, qui volunt et curam habent suz salutis, possunt discere. Sed et que est Ephesi ecclesia a Paulo quidem fundata, Johanne autem permanente apud eos usque ad Trajani tempora, testis est verus Apostolorum traditionis,
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the plan of the Apostles, made manifest in the whole world, is present for all to see in every Church, and we have the ability to count those who were appointed by the Apostles as bishops in the churches, and their successions up to us, who taught nothing like what these people rave about. For if the Apostles had known secret mysteries, which they taught separately and in secret to the perfect ones, they would have handed them down especially to those to whom they also entrusted the churches. They wanted them to be very strong and blameless in all things, to whom they left their own place of teaching, so that great benefit would come to those who acted correctly, but the greatest calamity to those who fell away. But since it is very long to enumerate the successions of all the churches in this kind of book, we will indicate the tradition that the church, which was founded and established by the most glorious Apostles Peter and Paul at Rome, has from the Apostles, and the faith announced to men, which comes down to us through the successions of bishops. We confound all those who in any way, whether through self-pleasing or empty glory or through blindness and bad judgment, gather apart from what is proper. For it is necessary for every church to agree with this church, that is, with those who are faithful from all over, in which the tradition that is from the Apostles has always been preserved. The blessed Apostles, therefore, founding and building the Church, handed over the episcopate to Linus to administer the Church. Paul mentions this Linus in the letters to Timothy. Anacletus succeeds him, and in the third place from the Apostles, Clement receives the episcopate, who also saw the Apostles themselves and conversed with them, and who had before his eyes the preaching of the Apostles and their tradition, not alone, for many were still alive at that time who had been taught by the Apostles. Under him, therefore, a not insignificant dissension having arisen among the brothers who were at Corinth, the Church of Rome wrote very powerful letters to the Corinthians, gathering them to peace and restoring their faith and announcing the tradition that it had recently received from the Apostles, announcing one God, omnipotent, maker of heaven and earth, shaper of man, who brought about the flood, and called Abraham, who led the people out of the land of Egypt, who spoke with Moses, who gave the law, and sent the prophets, who prepared fire for the devil and his angels. This Father of our Lord Jesus Christ is announced by the churches from the scripture itself, and those who wish to learn can understand the apostolic tradition of the Church, since the letter is older than those who now falsely teach and invent another God over the Demiurge and maker of all these things. To this Clement, Evaristus succeeds, and to Evaristus Alexander, and next Sixtus was established sixth from the Apostles, and from him Telesphorus, who also gloriously suffered martyrdom, and next Hyginus, then Pius, then Anicetus. When Soter succeeded Anicetus, now in the twelfth place, Eleutherius has the episcopate from the Apostles. This ordination and succession shows that the tradition that is from the Apostles in the Church and the proclamation of truth is one and the same and has come down to us. And Polycarpus, who was not only taught by the Apostles and conversed with many of those who saw our Lord, but was also established as bishop in the church of Smyrna in Asia by the Apostles, whom we also saw in our early years, for he persevered much and as a very old man gloriously and nobly suffered martyrdom, always taught what he had learned from the Apostles, which are the only true things. The churches in Asia and those who have succeeded Polycarpus up to now bear witness to these things, who is a man of much greater authority and more faithful to the truth than Valentinus and Marcion and the rest who are of perverse judgment. For he is the one who, when he came to the city under Anicetus, converted many of those heretics to the Church of God, announcing the one and only truth that he had perceived from the Apostles, which he also handed down to the Church. And there are those who heard him, for when John, the disciple of the Lord, was going to bathe in Ephesus and saw Cerinthus inside, he ran out of the bath unbathed, saying that he feared the bath would collapse, since Cerinthus, the enemy of truth, was inside. And Polycarpus himself, when Marcion once met him and said, 'Do you recognize us?', replied, 'I recognize you as the firstborn of Satan.' The Apostles and their disciples had such fear that they did not even communicate with any of those who had corrupted the truth, just as Paul also says: 'Avoid a heretical man after one correction, knowing that he who is such is perverse and is condemned by himself.' There is also a letter of Polycarpus to the Philippians, written perfectly, from which those who wish to learn and have care for their salvation can understand the character of his faith and the proclamation of truth. But also the church in Ephesus, which was founded by Paul and in which John remained until the time of Trajan, is a true witness to the tradition of the Apostles.

pass_b_english: The plan of the Apostles stands open to view in every church throughout the world, for all who truly desire to see it; we can trace the bishops appointed by the Apostles and their unbroken succession down to our own day, and none of them ever taught the fancies these people now proclaim. If the Apostles had possessed secret mysteries, reserved for a select few and taught in private, they would surely have entrusted them above all to those to whom they also committed the care of the churches. They wanted those successors to be steadfast and blameless in everything, so that their right stewardship of the apostolic office would bring great benefit, while their failure would bring utter disaster. But to list the succession of every church would swell this work beyond measure; therefore we set forth the tradition of that greatest and most ancient church, known to all, which the two most glorious Apostles Peter and Paul founded and established at Rome, and the faith it has handed down to humanity through the succession of its bishops. By this we confound all who, whether from self-will, empty pride, blindness, or perverse judgment, gather apart from the true communion. For every church must agree with this church — that is, with the faithful everywhere — because in it the tradition from the Apostles has been preserved without interruption. (cf. 1 Tim 1:20; Titus 3:10)

Having founded and built the Church, the blessed Apostles entrusted its oversight to Linus; Paul himself mentions Linus in his letters to Timothy. After Linus came Anacletus, and third from the Apostles, Clement received the episcopate — a man who had seen the Apostles, conversed with them, and held their living preaching and tradition before his eyes. He was not alone in this; many who had been taught by the Apostles were still alive. When a serious dispute broke out among the brothers at Corinth, the Church of Rome sent a most powerful letter to restore peace, renew their faith, and proclaim the tradition it had recently received from the Apostles: one God, almighty, maker of heaven and earth, fashioner of man, who sent the flood, called Abraham, led his people out of Egypt, spoke with Moses, gave the law, sent the prophets, and prepared fire for the devil and his angels. This Father of our Lord Jesus Christ is proclaimed by the churches from Scripture itself; those who wish to learn can recognize the apostolic tradition there, for this letter is older than those who now falsely teach and invent another God above the Demiurge and Creator of all things.

After Clement came Evaristus, then Alexander; sixth from the Apostles came Sixtus, then Telesphorus, who gloriously suffered martyrdom; then Hyginus, then Pius, then Anicetus. When Soter succeeded Anicetus, Eleutherius now holds the episcopate in the twelfth place from the Apostles. This ordered succession demonstrates that the tradition from the Apostles in the Church and the proclamation of truth are one and the same, and have come down to us intact — proving that the life-giving faith preserved and handed on in the Church from the Apostles until now is one and the same.

Polycarp, too, was not only taught by the Apostles and familiar with many who had seen the Lord, but was appointed bishop of the church at Smyrna in Asia by the Apostles themselves. We saw him in our early years; he endured to a great age and departed this life by a glorious and noble martyrdom. He always taught what he had learned from the Apostles — teachings that alone are true. All the churches in Asia and those who have succeeded Polycarp to this day bear witness to this; he is a man of far greater authority and a more faithful witness to the truth than Valentinus, Marcion, and the rest of their perverse school. When he came to Rome under Anicetus, he converted many of the heretics we have mentioned to the Church of God, proclaiming the one truth he had received from the Apostles and handed on to the Church. There are those who heard him tell how John, the Lord's disciple, once went to bathe in Ephesus, saw Cerinthus inside, and rushed out unbathed, saying he feared the bathhouse would collapse because the enemy of truth was within. And when Marcion once confronted Polycarp and asked, "Do you recognize us?" he answered, "I recognize you as the firstborn of Satan." Such was the dread the Apostles and their disciples had of any communion, even in word, with those who corrupted the truth — just as Paul commands: "Avoid a divisive person after a first and second warning, knowing that such a one is warped and self-condemned." (Titus 3:10; cf. 1 Tim 1:20) Polycarp also wrote an excellent letter to the Philippians, from which those who desire to learn and care for their salvation can discern the character of his faith and his proclamation of truth. The church at Ephesus, founded by Paul and where John remained until the time of Trajan, stands as a true witness to the tradition of the Apostles.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances, including the specific list of attributes of God and the succession of bishops. Scripture citations (Titus 3:10 and 1 Timothy 1:20) correctly identify the source of the quoted Pauline text 'Hareticum autem hominem post unam correptionem devita'.
